title: Adaptive similarity-aware prefix canonicalizer & ghost tombstone invalidation
creator: Jordan Park
description:
Problem: The embeddings/ rerank endpoint sees a high rate of near-duplicate prefix inputs (conversations, repeated boilerplate, minor edits). Recomputing embeddings for these similar prefixes wastes GPU cycles and increases tail latency under load. Current prefix dedup strategies are brittle to small edits and either miss hits (overly strict hashing) or mis-serve stale content (overly aggressive canonicalization).

Goal: Implement a shard-resident, similarity-aware prefix canonicalizer that groups near-duplicate inputs into canonical keys and maintains lightweight 'ghost' tombstones for invalidation when upstream content changes. Key goals are: 1) increase cache hit rate for semantically-similar prefixes with minimal false-positive collisions, 2) keep reranking quality unchanged (no silent regressions), 3) ensure P95/P99 latency degradations are <= 5ms for cache lookup path, and 4) scale to multi-tenant shards with bounded memory and predictable eviction behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype implemented behind feature flag in embeddings service (shard-local mode)
Benchmarked cache hit improvement: +40% effective hit-rate for near-duplicate workloads in 3 production-sampled traces
Quality regression check: rerank MRR and embedding cosine similarity stable within 0.5% vs baseline on regression suite
End-to-end P95 latency increase for cache path <= 5ms; P99 <= 10ms overhead
Tombstone invalidation correctly prevents serving stale canonical embeddings within 30s of upstream content change in high-write tenants
Operational metrics (per-shard memory, tombstone count, canonicalization collision rate) surfaced to Console dashboard
Feature flag and rollout plan to ramp to 25% traffic, with automatic rollback criteria defined
design_decisions: Use variable-length shingle tokenization (word- and byte-level) + SimHash (64-bit) to produce a similarity fingerprint instead of strict content hashing — balances recall vs precision for near-duplicates
Maintain two-tier keying: (1) canonical key = shortest stable prefix fingerprint; (2) content-hash (SHA256) for exact-match verification and tombstone lineage
Store canonical entries as small value pointers to tenant-scoped embedding blobs (S3-backed with LRU metadata in-memory per shard)
Tombstones are lightweight records with (content-hash, version, expiry_ts); stores will track tombstone vector per canonical key to invalidate stale pointers without immediate eviction
Eviction policy: hybrid windowed-LRU with tombstone-aware aging — tombstones accelerate eviction of stale canonical entries when memory pressure rises
Design favors shard-local state to avoid cross-shard coordination on hot paths; periodic background reconciliation syncs canonical->blob mapping to global index for migration and disaster recovery
Collision handling: on canonical fingerprint collision, verify with exact content-hash; if false positive, create separate canonical candidate and track split metrics for later tuning
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Initial spike design reviewed with Infra & SRE (Mei Chen). SRE flagged tombstone amplification risk under heavy update workloads; design updated to include adaptive expiry and rate-limited tombstone writes.
2026-03-04: Prototype implementing shingle tokenizer and SimHash created (branch feat/eng/98147-simhash). Local unit tests and fuzzing added for tokenizer edge cases.
2026-03-06: Microbenchmarks: fingerprint generation avg 0.32ms per request (p95 0.9ms) in Go service on m5.large. Memory overhead projected at ~1.8k per canonical entry (metadata only).
2026-03-07: Integration test with embedding pipeline: feature-flagged cache lookup reduced compute calls by 38% on chat sample trace A; regression tests running to validate rerank metrics.
2026-03-09: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/embedding-service/pull/4125 (prototype + feature flag). Requesting Eng + SRE review.
comments: Liam O'Connor (2026-03-03): Recommend adding a tenant-override opt-out for organizations with strict determinism requirements — added to acceptance criteria.
Mei Chen (SRE, 2026-03-05): Concerned about tombstone write amplification; suggested adaptive expiry and a throttle for high-update tenants — implemented as rate-limited tombstone writer in design.
Aisha Martinez (2026-03-08): Note on performance budget: try to inline fingerprinting into request path without additional syscall overhead; prefer preallocated buffers.
Design review requested from Mei & Liam; tagging PM for rollout coordination.
notes_for_rollout: Start disabled in stable runtime. Roll out to 5% of traffic for read-heavy tenants, monitor cache hit rate, tombstone growth, and rerank quality. Automatic rollback if rerank MRR drops >0.7% or tombstone count grows >3x baseline within 1 hour.
